why: Doc quote CONFIRMED verbatim: auto-mode-config.md:304 reads exactly 'When auto mode denies a tool call, Claude Code records the denial in `/permissions` under the **Recently denied** tab.' The whole line is two sentences and the second reinforces rather than reverses ('Press `r` on a denied action to mark it for retry: when you exit the dialog, Claude Code sends a message telling the model it may retry that tool call and resumes the conversation.'). So the finding is not a paraphrase. It is refuted on the other two checks. (1) CITED EVIDENCE IS WRONG AT THE LINE. packages/shared/src/i18n/locales/en.json:1503-1504 are 'settings.permissions.customApiEndpoint' / 'customBashPattern'; the sandbox-egress 'Denied' strings the finding describes are at :1515-1516 (settings.permissions.isolationEgressDenied / isolationEgressDeniedDesc). The substance of that half survives the drift -- `grep -ain Denied` over en.json returns exactly those two keys -- but the citation as filed does not say what was claimed. (2) THE GAP IS A RECORDED, REASONED, DELIBERATE EXCLUSION, not an unnoticed divergence. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-auto-mode-policy.md:430-437, under its own heading '## Deliberately out of scope', reads: 'The denial-review flow and `auto-mode` CLI subcommands -- a UI and CLI surface, not a decision path. Record them as follow-ups if Task 2's doc read confirms they are part of the contract.' That plan is the one that owns parity row R21 ('the auto-mode classifier ... with overridable block/allow rules, a denial-review flow and `auto-mode` CLI subcommands', audit line 674, closed done), and the plan's own Task 3 premise section at :47 already states the absence in the same words: 'No org policy, no trusted repos, buckets or domains, no denial-review flow.' Per AGENTS.md a plan is where a deviation's reason lives, so this is a decision with a reason. It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 -- I checked all nine; the nearest neighbour is #3, autoMode.classifyAllShell, a different key. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS OVERSTATED, which is this repo's named recurring false-positive shape. Denials ARE recorded, and a human CAN clear one: GuardianConsultState keeps a session-scoped bounded (GUARDIAN_DENIED_SET_MAX = 200, LRU-on-write) set of every (action, cwd) the judge denied (packages/shared/src/agent/core/guardian-consult.ts:139, recordDenied :193-200), and pi-agent.ts:4650-4658 arms guardian.recordPostDenialOverride whenever the user approves at a prompt an action the guardian denied earlier in the session -- that exact action is then never re-consulted. That is a user-facing review-and-allow of a prior denial; what is missing is only the USER-INITIATED browse-a-list-and-press-r shape, since the override is reached when the model re-attempts and the action lands at a prompt. The PermissionDenied `{retry:true}` hook the finding concedes is indeed live and bounded to MAX_PERMISSION_DENIED_RETRIES = 1 per tool call (pi-agent.ts:370, 4438-4470), with the matcher arm present (automations/utils.ts:173). (4) FORM FACTOR. `/permissions` is a Claude Code TUI slash-command dialog and `r` is a TUI keybinding; Nessy Desktop is an Electron GUI with a Settings > Permissions page and no slash-command permission dialog at all, and apps/cli is a thin websocket client with no interactive permission surface (no '/permissions' string anywhere in packages/ or apps/). The literal claimed affordance cannot exist in this fork's shape. Absence itself verified with `grep -rain` (NUL-safe) for 'recently denied' / recentlyDenied / recently-denied / denialHistory / deniedHistory / denialLog / markForRetry / retryDenied across packages/ and apps/: zero source hits, only the sweep's own JSON/markdown rows. Sibling-subsystem check: the one adjacent hit, thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction, is a generated Codex app-server protocol type (packages/codex-protocol/generated/), a different subsystem behind NESSY_FEATURE_CODEX_RUNTIME which is off by default -- naming it as our surface would be the wrong-subsystem error.
correctedState: Nessy Desktop has no browsable 'Recently denied' surface and no user-initiated mark-for-retry keypress, and that absence is a recorded deliberate exclusion, not an unnoticed gap: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-auto-mode-policy.md:430-437 scopes out 'the denial-review flow and `auto-mode` CLI subcommands' as 'a UI and CLI surface, not a decision path', and the plan's premise section :47 already recorded 'no denial-review flow' when parity row R21 was closed. The finding's stronger claims are false: auto-mode denials ARE recorded (GuardianConsultState's session-scoped bounded denied set, guardian-consult.ts:139/193-200), and a human CAN clear one -- approving at a prompt an action the guardian denied earlier arms recordPostDenialOverride so that action is never re-consulted for the session (pi-agent.ts:4650-4658) -- alongside the live PermissionDenied `{retry:true}` hook, bounded to one retry per tool call (pi-agent.ts:370, 4438-4470). The cited evidence line is also off: the only 'Denied' strings in en.json are the sandbox-egress labels at :1515-1516, not :1503-1504. What is genuinely missing is only the user-initiated review-a-denial-list affordance, which is TUI-shaped (`/permissions` dialog, `r` keypress) and has no counterpart in this GUI fork; if it is wanted it is a new Settings surface, and it is the follow-up the 2026-07-26 plan asked to record.
